content.thinking:
Alright, the recent series of edits have cleaned up the TUI component: I removed the unused `stream` state, trimmed the intro rendering logic, and tweaked the assistant message layout. The Bash commands I ran confirmed that the intro animation now plays correctly, the wordmark appears mid‑animation, and after the intro the tagline stays in the scrollback. So the interactive experience looks good when run directly via `bun run src/index.tsx`.

The next logical step is to verify that the production build also includes these changes. The project ships a script `scripts/build-logo.ts` that generates the ASCII logo assets used by the TUI. In development mode the logo is generated on the fly, but the compiled binary will embed whatever static assets the script produces at build time. Therefore I need to run that script first to ensure the latest logo is baked into the source.

After that, I should invoke the Bun build pipeline. The `bun build` command can compile the TypeScript entry point (`src/index.tsx`) into a single native executable (`dist/glint`). I’ll pass `--compile` to produce a binary, and `--outfile dist/glint` to place it in the `dist` folder. It’s useful to capture the tail of the build output (using `tail -5`) so I can see any warnings or errors without flooding the console. Finally, listing the contents of `dist/` with `ls -la` will confirm that the binary was actually created and give me its permissions and size.

Putting it all together, the appropriate Bash command is:

```
bun run scripts/build-logo.ts >/dev/null 2>&1;
bun build src/index.tsx --compile --outfile dist/glint 2>&1 | tail -5 && ls -la dist/
```

This will (1) generate the logo assets silently, (2) build the binary while capturing the last few lines of output, and (3) show the resulting file in `dist/`. Executing this will let me confirm that the compiled binary contains the updated intro/logo and is ready for distribution.
